sentences.text: Tylocephale is a genus of dinosaur belonging to the group Pachycephalosauria, which is part of the larger Marginocephalia clade.
The only known species, T. gilmorei, bears the name of American paleontologist Charles Gilmore for his early detailed work on these dinosaurs.
This animal was average-sized for its group, reaching two meters in length and forty kilograms in mass, yet it possesses the tallest known dome among pachycephalosaurs.
Its head features an array of spikes, nodes, and tubercules behind the dome, and the structure includes fused sutures and expanded squamosal shelves similar to Pachycephalosaurus.
Fossils were unearthed between 1965 and 1971 at the Khulsan locality in the Barun Goyot Formation of the Gobi Desert by a Polish-Mongolian Expedition.
Teresa Maryańska and Halszka Osmólska described the type species as a new genus and species in 1974 based on a partial skull and mandible.
Serrations on the teeth suggest a diet that might include leaves, nuts, seeds, and insects, though it is debated whether this implies a truly heterogeneous menu.
Some researchers propose a back-and-forth jaw motion unlike Stegoceras, while others debate if older individuals could head-butt given potential healing issues in their domes.
Tylocephale lived in what is now Mongolia during the Early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 72 to 71 million years ago.
